REPORT ON ARREST OF A JAPANESE AND A KOREAN ARMS SMUGGLERS
BY JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE

Made by J. D. I. Nakagawa Forwarded by

Sir,

With reference to the articles appearing in the
Shanghai Mainichi dated March 28, one referring to the
arrest of a Japanese named H. Fukuda and another to that of
a Korean named Chang Chi Tsai(張基贊), I beg respectfully
to report that my enquiries have confirmed the authenticity
of both reports.

H. Fukuda is known both to the Municipal Police and
the Japanese Consular Police as a notorious smuggler of
firearms. He was arrested by Japanese detectives attached
to Hongkew Station in December 1925 on a charge of illicit
transactions in firearms and was later sentenced at the
Japanese Court to 20 days' imprisonment and deportation
from China for a period of 5 years on the expiration of
the prison term.

According to the Japanese authorities Fukuda came to
Shanghai in January this year and has been residing at
1400 Tao Yuen Li off Yangtszepoo Road. He was arrested
on March 26 on a warrant issued by the Nagasaki Police
for being implicated in an illicit deal in firearms with
other accomplices who are now under arrest at Nagasaki.
He was escorted to Nagasaki on the N. Y. K. liner Nagasaki
Maru which sailed for Japan at 9 a.m. on March 29 to be
tried together with his confederates.

Chang Chi Tsai was arrested by Inspector Sugimura on
March 27 on Woochang Road where the Inspector accidentally

关于日本领事警察逮捕一名日本人和一名朝鲜人军火走私犯的报告

由 J. D. I. 中川（Nakagawa）呈报 转呈

阁下：

鉴于3月28日《上海每日新闻》（Shanghai Mainichi）刊登的文章，其中一篇提及一名名为 H. Fukuda 的日本人被捕，另一篇提及一名名为 Chang Chi Tsai（張基贊）的朝鲜人被捕，本人谨此报告，经查询已证实这两则报道均属实。

H. Fukuda 被公共租界警务处及日本领事警察公认为臭名昭著的枪支走私犯。他于1925年12月因非法交易枪支罪被隶属于虹口巡捕房的日本侦探逮捕，随后被日本法院判处监禁20天，并在刑满后被驱逐出中国，为期5年。

据日本当局称，Fukuda 于今年1月来到上海，一直居住在杨树浦路陶源里1400号。他于3月26日持长崎警察签发的逮捕令被捕，原因是涉嫌与其他同伙进行非法枪支交易，这些同伙目前已在长崎被捕。他被护送上日本邮船会社（N. Y. K.）的“长崎丸”号（Nagasaki Maru）轮船，该轮于3月29日上午9时启航前往日本，他将在那里与同伙一并受审。

Chang Chi Tsai 于3月27日在武昌路被杉村（Sugimura）巡官逮捕，当时该巡官偶然

MISCELLANEOUS 7 ARMED ROBBERS, MEMBERS OF GANG OPERATING IN
JAPANESE HOUSES NOW UNDER ARREST: EXCELLENT WORK BY THE
HONGKEW POLICE

The Shanghai Mainichi, Shanghai Nichi Nichi and the
Shanghai Nippo publish the following report:-
As a result of untiring efforts on the part of the
detectives attached to Hongkew Police Station 7 men, believed
to be members of the gang of armed robbers which has recently
been operating in Japanese houses in both eastern and
western mill districts, were arrested in Urfa Road on March
25. These men are said to have confessed to many armed
robberies committed in the Settlement both in Japanese and
Chinese houses. One of the men was identified yesterday
by Mrs. J. Yamamoto, the lady who was shot in the abdomen
some time ago in one of the quarters of the No. 14 mill of
the Naigwai Wata Kaisha and who is still an inmate in the
Foo King Hospital. Complainants in cases committed in
the eastern mill district and in another case in North
Szechuen Road Extension, however, were unable to identify
any of the men. It is believed that other members of the
gang whom the Police are trailing are responsible for these
crimes. A fully-loaded .32 calibre automatic pistol was
found on the person of one of the robbers at the time of
his arrest.
According to a confession made by the men in custody,
their gang is connected with the group of assassins
of the Communist Party.
...............................
-do- NOTORIOUS ARMS TRAFFICKER UNDER ARREST

The Shanghai Mainichi publishes the following reports:-
K. Fukuda, a notorious smuggler of firearms residing
at 1300 Sze Yuer Li off Yangtzepoo Road, was taken into
custody by the Japanese Police on March 24. It is believed
that Japanese authorities received a cable from Nagasaki
Police which implicated Fukuda in a certain illicit
transaction in firearms.
...............................
KOREAN ARMS SMUGGLER ARRESTED FOR RETURNING TO SHANGHAI

Yesterday, Inspector Sugimura of the Japanese Consular
Police accidentally run across a Korean named Chang Chi
Tsai(張基贊) on Woochang Road and arrested him for
returning to Shanghai. Chang was deported from his town on
December 1, 1928 after having served a prison term on a
charge of illicit dealing in firearms. He returned to
Shanghai about a week ago and has been residing under the
alias A. Okamura.
...............................
-dc- 700 JAPANESE PLUMJACKETS TO LEAVE FOR JAPAN TO-MORROW

The Shanghai Nippo publishes the following report:-
The relief parties having arrived here a few days ago,
700 Japanese sailors attached to the Naval Landing Forces
will sail for home on the transport Takasaki which leaves
here at noon to-morrow.

杂项 7 名武装劫匪，系在日本人家中作案的团伙成员，现已被捕：虹口警方功绩卓著

《上海每日新闻》、《上海日日新闻》（Shanghai Nichi Nichi）和《上海新报》（Shanghai Nippo）刊登了以下报道：-
由于隶属于虹口巡捕房的侦探们不懈努力，3月25日在乌尔法路（Urfa Road）逮捕了7名男子，据信他们是近期在东、西纱厂区日本人家中作案的武装抢劫团伙成员。据说这些人供认了在租界内日本人和中国人家中犯下的多起武装抢劫案。其中一人昨日被山本（J. Yamamoto）夫人指认，山本夫人此前在内海棉业株式会社（Naigwai Wata Kaisha）第十四厂宿舍之一腹部中枪，目前仍在福金医院（Foo King Hospital）住院治疗。然而，发生在东纱厂区以及北四川路延伸段另一起案件的报案人未能指认出任何嫌疑人。据信，警方正在追踪的该团伙其他成员应对这些罪行负责。在逮捕其中一名劫匪时，从其身上搜出一支装满子弹的 .32 口径自动手枪。
根据在押人员的供词，他们的团伙与共产党刺客集团有关联。
...............................
-同上- 臭名昭著的军火贩子被捕

《上海每日新闻》刊登了以下报道：-
居住于杨树浦路四越里1300号的臭名昭著的枪支走私犯 K. Fukuda，于3月24日被日本警察拘留。据信，日本当局收到了来自长崎警察的电报，指控 Fukuda 参与某起非法枪支交易。
...............................
朝鲜军火走私犯因返回上海被捕

昨日，日本领事警察杉村（Sugimura）巡官在武昌路偶然遇到一名名为 Chang Chi Tsai（張基贊）的朝鲜人，并以其返回上海为由将其逮捕。Chang 曾因非法买卖枪支罪服刑，并于1928年12月1日刑满后被驱逐出其所在城镇。他约于一周前返回上海，一直化名 A. Okamura 居住。
...............................
-dc- 700名日本水兵明日启程返日

《上海新报》刊登了以下报道：-
救援部队已于数日前抵达此地，隶属于海军陆战队的700名日本水兵将乘坐运输舰“高崎丸”号（Takasaki）回国，该舰将于明日中午从此地启航。
